exports.text: Raw 64-bit layer provides masked-clear fetch, bitwise OR/XOR updates with silent and prior-value forms, unconditional exchange, three-way compare exchange, and boolean compare exchange with caller expectation refresh, each across full, acquire, release and relaxed orderings.

Raw 64-bit layer provides zero tests after subtract, decrement and increment, signed negativity test after add with ordering variants, and guarded arithmetic that skips update on a forbidden value or sign and reports prior content, result, or success.

Instrumented 32-bit layer exposes acquire/plain loads, plain/release stores, add/sub/inc/dec with new-value and prior-value reports, AND/ANDNOT/OR/XOR with silent and reporting forms, exchange and both compare-exchange styles, plus arithmetic tests and guarded updates, validating access then delegating.

Instrumented 64-bit layer exposes plain/acquire loads, plain/release stores, add/sub/inc/dec with silent, new-value and prior-value families, bitwise AND/ANDNOT/OR/XOR with silent and reporting forms, exchange, both compare-exchange styles, arithmetic tests, and guarded updates with ordering suffixes.

Long layer abstracts word width for reads, stores, arithmetic, bitwise, exchange and compare exchange, with instrumented entries recording access and forwarding to same-shaped raw helpers that select the wide or narrow fixed-width implementation at compile time.

Long layer also covers masked-clear and XOR reporting forms, subtract/decrement/increment tests, ordered negativity checks, and conditional add/increment/decrement guards, each instrumented entry propagating the matching raw helper outcome.

hazards.text: Bitwise fetch OR/XOR have no generic software fallback and fail translation when the architecture supplies neither the ordered nor the relaxed form, unlike exchange, compare exchange and test helpers that degrade to simpler primitives.

Holder compare forms touch two caller objects: the holder must stay valid and writable for the call and must match machine-word size and alignment because the long layer reinterprets it through a width-specific signed type.
Ordering suffix selects both the delegated primitive and the checking marker, so substituting one suffix for another silently changes the cross-thread visibility contract.

invariants.text: Missing ordered forms are assembled from relaxed work plus fences: full uses fences on both sides, acquire adds a trailing acquire fence, release adds a leading release fence; native ordered forms are preferred when present.

Derived raw operations reuse simpler ones: masked clear via inverted-mask clear-set, zero tests via equality of a returning result against zero, negativity via signed comparison, guarded add via prior-value comparison, nonzero-guarded increment via guarded add of one.

Instrumented wrappers annotate before delegating: loads read-only, stores write-only, updates read-write over the whole object, and holder compare forms additionally mark the caller holder; full reporting and test forms add a full barrier mark, release forms a release mark, others none.
Raw long helpers preserve operation, operands and ordering while selecting the 64-bit counterpart on 64-bit builds and the narrower counterpart otherwise, with identical arity and result forwarding.
Wrappers add only checking and marking and establish no mutual exclusion, inheriting atomicity and visibility from the raw primitives; the instrumented header carries a multiple-inclusion guard.

Instrumented wrappers depend on external access-marking helpers for atomic read, write, combined access and generic holder access, plus external full-barrier and release checking markers, invoked before delegation; their internals are outside this dossier.

state_machines.text: Guarded updates loop from an observed value: exit when the guard holds, else try storing a computed successor and retry with the refreshed observation until guard or success; boolean compare exchange refreshes caller expectation only on failure and reports equality.

structs.text: A 64-bit atomic value lives in a container exposing a 64-bit integer member addressed directly by generic exchange and compare-exchange fallbacks.
